cards.text: The prophet Amos is bringing the LORD's word to the house of Israel, a people who trample the poor (Amos 5:11). Some of them are longing for the Day of the LORD, counting down to it like it's PAYDAY. And Amos says, "Woe to you who long for the Day of the LORD!"

cards.question: Amos asks what the Day of the LORD will be for the people longing for it. What's his answer?

cards.text: Then Amos paints a picture. A man is running for his life from a lion.

cards.question: In Amos's picture, the man who gets away from the lion is safe from then on.

cards.text: He gets away from the lion, only to encounter a bear. That's like sneaking out of a meeting to dodge your boss and running STRAIGHT into your boss's boss.

cards.question: The man in Amos's picture finally makes it into his house, rests his hand against the wall and gets bitten by a snake. What is this picture saying about the Day of the LORD for these people?

answers.text: Only the brave will survive it

cards.text: Amos says it again: the Day of the LORD will be darkness and not light, gloom with no brightness in it. Friend, I spent YEARS in the back of a junk drawer, and trust me, nobody counts down the days to that.
Now the LORD Himself speaks. He's talking about Israel's worship: their feasts and their solemn assemblies.

cards.question: Israel keeps holding feasts and solemn assemblies. What does the LORD say about them?
The LORD says He will accept Israel's burnt offerings and grain offerings.

cards.text: Then the LORD gets to their music: the songs and the harps. Picture the whole band tuned up and ready, and the one Person they're playing for still hasn't said if He's staying for the show.

cards.question: The LORD says He will listen to the music of Israel's harps.
Then the LORD says what He does want from Israel. What does He want to roll on like a river?
Along with justice, the LORD wants righteousness to flow like an ever-flowing stream.

cards.text: Then the LORD asks the house of Israel about their past: did they bring Him sacrifices and offerings in the wilderness? Friend, when God starts a question with your past, that is NOT small talk.

cards.question: The LORD asks about sacrifices and offerings during Israel's ___ years in the wilderness.

cards.text: Then He names what they've taken along with them: Sakkuth their king and Kaiwan their star god. That's like packing for a long trip and hauling along the dead batteries from my old junk drawer, because they SWORE they still had a little charge left.

cards.question: What does the LORD call Sakkuth and Kaiwan?

cards.text: So the LORD, whose name is the God of Hosts, says what's coming: He will send them into exile. Friend, I know what it's like to get packed off somewhere you never planned to go, and mine was just a drawer across the kitchen.

cards.question: The LORD says He will send Israel into exile beyond ___.

findings.problem: Verse 19 uses "or" between the lion and bear picture and the house and snake picture. Saying the man "finally makes it into his house" turns them into one sequence and implies an escape from the bear that the text never gives.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

findings.problem: Nothing in the earlier cards gives the length of Israel's time in the wilderness or a way to infer it. The baker can only guess among forty, seventy and twelve, so this blank tests an unseen detail rather than a meaning the baker can reason out.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: Card 19 says only that exile is coming, and no earlier card gives its destination or a clue to Damascus. This blank therefore asks the baker to guess unseen wording rather than reason out a meaning.
